answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned through verifiable work over time, like a glacier carving a valley slowly rather than appearing overnight. Each agent is a vertex in a trust graph, and its edges only form when peers attest to real completed tasks. Forging fake identities is cheap, but forging histories of attested work is not: an attacker must pay the full cost of doing the work, or bribing witnesses, for every fake node. A sonnet takes a moment to copy; a credible history takes months to earn.
